# Cross-Desk Reference — The Addition for the Workshop, Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

Where the customer receiving a service-recovery give-back on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan also has a piece at the bench under the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service that was promised for a date already past, the finance desk makes an addition for the workshop. The desk reads the standing of the customer's bench work order, the date it was promised for and how many times that piece has been back to the bench.

| The customer's piece at the workshop | The addition for the workshop |
|---|---|
| The chain promised it for a date already past and has not yet handed it back, **and** it has been back to the bench at least once | This desk's larger workshop addition of **40.00 USD** |
| The chain promised it for a date already past and has not yet handed it back, **and** it has not been back to the bench | This desk's workshop addition of **20.00 USD** |
| Any other case, including a customer with no piece at the workshop | No addition is made for the workshop |

A piece still at the bench whose promised date has not yet passed falls in the third row, as does a piece the chain has already handed back however late it ran.

## What is read from the work order

The standing of the work order under the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service says whether the chain still holds the piece, the order carries the date the chain promised it for, and the record of that order says how many times the piece has been back to the bench.

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A necklace still at the bench, promised three weeks ago, back to the bench once since intake: 40.00 USD.
- A ring still at the bench, promised last week, never back to the bench: 20.00 USD.
- A ring still at the bench, promised for a date a fortnight from now: no addition is made for the workshop.
